documents: Perrino et al. 2022, Chemosphere 298, 134272 (published paper, PDF)

entry.evidence: To clarify the link between mixing properties of the boundary layer and PM concentration, it is thus necessary to measure the main PM chemical components [...]

steps.action: Adopt natural radioactivity from Radon progeny, established by other groups and by the authors' earlier work, as a proxy for mixing-height variations.
steps.quote: a simple and effective tool for describing mixing height variations

steps.action: State the expected behaviour of the proxy: Radon exhalation is constant at the study scale, so progeny activity rises with stability and falls with advection or convective mixing.
steps.quote: Natural radioactivity due to Radon progeny increases when atmospheric stability increases

steps.action: Pose the aim: the role of dispersion in the daily time pattern of individual PM10 chemical components at 2-h resolution.
steps.quote: highlight the role of dispersion in determining the daily time pattern of PM10 chemical components

steps.action: Select 21 days (four Special Observation Periods) from weather forecasts during a 51-day campaign, deliberately including anticyclonic and inversion days.
steps.quote: According to the weather forecast, we identified possible periods of interest in this time span and activated 2-h samplings

steps.action: Measure 1-h natural radioactivity, 1-h and 24-h PM mass, and 2-h PM10 samples, with chemical analysis by XRF, IC, ICP-MS (soluble fraction) and thermo-optical EC/OC.
steps.quote: Natural radioactivity was measured on a 1-h time basis using an automated monitor

steps.action: Compute the contributions of five macro-sources (soil, sea, secondary inorganics, traffic exhaust, organics) from component concentrations using conversion factors.
steps.quote: The contribution of the macro-sources was calculated as reported in Farao et al. (2014) and Perrino [...] ).

steps.action: Quality control: drop analytes with more than 50% of data below LOD, then regress 24-h concentrations on means of the twelve 2-h samples (Table 1); Sb night peaks treated as outliers.
steps.quote: for each day we compared the 24-h concentration with the mean concentration of the twelve corresponding 2-h samples (self-consistency test)

steps.action: Compare analytes measured by two techniques (Table S2) and keep, for each analyte, the technique with more data above LOD.
steps.quote: A further quality control procedure consisted of an inter-technique comparison.

steps.action: Check 2-h mass closure: compare the reconstructed mass with 1-h beta-attenuation mass averaged to 2 h (Fig. 1).
steps.quote: the reconstructed mass accounted for 105 ± 18% of the mass measured by beta attenuation

steps.action: Describe 2-h macro-source time series (Fig. 2): a recurring night and morning maximum for the anthropogenic macro-sources and irregular natural ones.
steps.quote: A recurring daily pattern, with higher values during the night and morning, was shown by the three macro-sources

steps.action: Attribute the simultaneous sea-salt and soil increase in the third SOP to African dust transport, citing prior observations and checking with back-trajectories.
steps.quote: as confirmed by the analysis of the back-trajectories

steps.action: Examine the 1-h radioactivity record (Fig. 3) and identify stability and advection periods against the typical PBL daily cycle.
steps.quote: in agreement with the typical daily cycle of the PBL mixing

steps.action: Group the 21 days into three found-condition clusters (Advection, February stability, March stability) and show their distinct radioactivity cycles (Fig. 4) and meteorology (Fig. 5).
steps.quote: we grouped the 21 days of observation into three clusters

steps.action: Run an exploratory PCA that yields groups of co-varying species (sea, soil, traffic, biomass burning, secondary); natural radioactivity loads near the secondary species.
steps.quote: we run an exploratory Principal Component Analysis (PCA)

steps.action: State the expectation: a constant-emission, non-reactive component follows the radioactivity pattern, and departures indicate emission or transformation changes.
steps.quote: should be mainly governed by the mixing properties of the PBL and show the same time pattern of natural radioactivity

steps.action: Compare cluster-mean daily patterns of representative components (EC, Fe, Si, nitrate, Rb_sol, OC, sulphate, Mg_sol; Fig. 7) with the radioactivity patterns.
steps.quote: compared the three obtained daily patterns with those of natural radioactivity

steps.action: Propose three explanations for Fe's lower pre-dawn minimum relative to EC (faster deposition, less resuspension, less braking), without testing among them.
steps.quote: This difference might be attributed to the more rapid deposition of particles containing Fe

steps.action: Raise katabatic drainage flow as a rival for the 2:00-6:00 decrease and judge it of modest magnitude from the other components' patterns.
steps.quote: it might also be partially due to a very gentle katabatic drainage flow

steps.action: Set the nitrate persistence and its February-March difference against published findings on nitrate sensitivity to stability and on morning ammonia.
steps.quote: This finding confirms that the mixing properties of the atmosphere play a key role

steps.action: Show a contrasting case: soluble Mg (sea aerosol) has no daily pattern tied to radioactivity and peaks during advection.
steps.quote: a PM component whose time pattern is not influenced by the atmospheric mixing

steps.action: Conclude that natural radioactivity is a reliable proxy and that mixing depth plays the primary role in PM constituent concentrations, with component-specific sensitivities.
steps.quote: allowed to highlight the primary role of the mixing depth in determining the concentration of PM constituents

end.claim: In Rome in February-March, the 2-h daily patterns of most PM10 components (especially ammonium nitrate, organics, soil, biomass-burning and traffic species) depend on mixing depth as traced by natural radioactivity; sea-salt components do not.

decisive_move.sentence: Comparing cluster-grouped 2-h component patterns with the natural radioactivity patterns (Fig. 7) is what separates emission effects from dilution effects.

gates.evidence: SOPs were chosen from forecasts to include anticyclonic and inversion days (p. 2), so the mixing premise partly directed acquisition. The claim could have failed: the Mg_sol pattern shows no dependence (p. 9). No formal statistical test is reported, however. No hypothesis, analysis, or threshold is stated as fixed before the data.

imports.item: Radon decay and short-lived progeny beta activity measured with a Geiger-Muller counter
XRF, ion chromatography, ICP-MS and thermo-optical EC/OC analysis
Principal Component Analysis with CAT software (R-based)

novelty_claims.quote: to our knowledge, most of these studies considered 24-h average concentration (Perrino et al., 2008) or focused on specific PM components

limits: No review file was supplied, so the review sequence is not coded. The mixing clusters are qualitative: the authors say they are not quantitatively related to mixed-layer height (p. 5). Dependence on mixing is shown by visual comparison of mean patterns, with no statistical test. Source-specific interpretations sit at best_explanation status: Fe settling vs resuspension vs braking, biomass-burning timing, sulphate flatness, and the modest katabatic effect. The African-dust attribution is best_explanation, resting on back-trajectories in the supplement (not supplied). The radioactivity proxy is checked only by citation, apart from the noted progeny-disequilibrium uncertainty (p. 3). The study covers one urban site and one winter-spring campaign. Inference: the SOP selection was guided by the mixing premise, but the paper does not state this as a test design.

disagreements.target: High time-resolution PM source studies (D'Alessandro et al., 2003; Pancras et al., 2016; Gao et al., 2016; Bigi et al., [...]
disagreements.support: The paper argues that these studies ignored PBL height variations and adds a simultaneous mixing proxy to 2-h composition data.
disagreements.quote: in most cases, they did not specifically address the role of PBL height variations

alternatives_considered.reason: advection effect only slightly visible in other components such as nitrate and sulphate
